response.sql: WITH album_stats AS (SELECT AlbumId, SUM(Bytes) * 1.0 / SUM(Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track GROUP BY AlbumId), overall AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS mean_rate FROM album_stats), above AS (SELECT a.rate, a.track_count, a.rate - o.mean_rate AS excess FROM album_stats a CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE a.rate > o.mean_rate) SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate, AVG(track_count) AS avg_track_count, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: The rate's denominator is the total Milliseconds of all tracks in the album. Only the Bytes sum skips missing sizes, so tracks with NULL Bytes still contribute their duration.
Albums whose tracks all lack Bytes have a NULL rate. AVG ignores them, so they are excluded from the mean rate and from the above-mean set.
Track counts include every track in the album, including tracks with missing Bytes.
Tracks with NULL AlbumId form one group through GROUP BY and count as one album in the mean. The request states this.
Division is floating-point (*1.0) so rates are not truncated to integers, and no rounding is applied.

alternatives.interpretation: Tracks with missing Bytes are dropped from the album entirely, so their Milliseconds are excluded from the denominator as well as their Bytes from the numerator.
alternatives.sql: WITH album_stats AS (SELECT AlbumId, SUM(Bytes) * 1.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN Milliseconds END) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track GROUP BY AlbumId), overall AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS mean_rate FROM album_stats), above AS (SELECT a.rate, a.track_count, a.rate - o.mean_rate AS excess FROM album_stats a CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE a.rate > o.mean_rate) SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate, AVG(track_count) AS avg_track_count, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess FROM above;
